topStories.headline: Supervisors Unanimously Back Expansion of Downtown SF Partnership to 70 Blocks
topStories.dek: Jackson Square, Embarcadero Plaza, and the Ferry Building are now officially part of the Downtown SF Partnership's service area after a unanimous Board of Supervisors vote.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on July 22 to approve a sweeping expansion of the Downtown SF Partnership (DSFP), the community benefit district that funds street cleaning, safety ambassadors, and neighborhood activations across the Financial District. The vote formalizes a boundary expansion that stretches the district from 43 city blocks to 70, folding in Jackson Square, Embarcadero Plaza, and the Ferry Building for the first time.

Property owners backed the initiative with an 85% vote in favor, representing 61% of the district by square footage — a threshold observers called remarkable given the proposal asks building owners to tax themselves at higher rates. The new 10-year management agreement is set to launch operations in January 2027, following collection of fiscal year 2026–2027 assessments.

The enlarged district is designed to reflect downtown's post-pandemic geography, which now includes a concentration of AI offices and high-end retail in Jackson Square as well as a new public-private park being developed along the Embarcadero. The DSFP had been operating under a management plan formed in 2019 that stakeholders said no longer matched the neighborhood's evolving needs, particularly after city grant funding to the organization dropped by 70% in FY26 due to budget constraints.

Supervisor Danny Sauter, who represents the downtown area, noted the scale of the achievement. The expanded partnership will also double its annual budget, enabling more robust programming and services across all included neighborhoods.

topStories.headline: SF Centre Mall Deal Collapses, Leaving 1.2 Million-Square-Foot Property Back on the Market
topStories.dek: The shuttered former Westfield mall near Union Square is without a buyer again after local developers Presidio Bay and Prado Group walked away from their acquisition agreement.
topStories.body:
A high-profile plan to redevelop the shuttered San Francisco Centre mall has unraveled. Presidio Bay Ventures and Prado Group, the two local development firms that were selected as the winning bidders in March 2026, announced they are exiting the transaction, according to reporting by the SF Standard and SFist. The news puts the 1.2 million-square-foot property — which went fully dark early this year after its final tenants received eviction notices in late 2025 — back on the market with no clear buyer.

The collapse appears tied to multiple complications, including the unusual land-ownership structure beneath the mall: the underlying ground is owned by San Francisco Unified School District, which significantly complicates any residential conversion proposal. The mall had exited receivership late last year after Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase foreclosed on a $560 million outstanding loan tied to the prior owner, Westfield.

Speculation about the building's future has included concepts ranging from a soccer stadium to lab space to mixed-use redevelopment. Less than 10% of the property was leased at the time of its closure, according to CoStar. The property's bondholders, who are now effectively the sellers, had not announced next steps as of press time.

The news is a setback for Union Square's recovery narrative. Several blocks away, the Macy's flagship store on Stockton Street remains another potential redevelopment site, with developer TMG Partners in discussions about its future. City officials and retail brokers have pointed to other positive signs in the district, including a retail vacancy rate that has dropped from a peak of 22% in 2025 to around 15% this year.

topStories.headline: Office-to-Housing Pipeline Builds Steam in Downtown Core
topStories.dek: A wave of conversion applications is expected this month as the city's Downtown Revitalization Financing District begins attracting serious developer interest.
topStories.body:
Nearly six months after Mayor Daniel Lurie signed the Downtown Revitalization Financing District (DRFD) into law in February 2026, the office-to-housing conversion pipeline is showing real momentum. Three projects totaling approximately 300 units are expected to submit applications to the city this month, according to Planetizen and Axios reporting, with city planners identifying roughly 48 buildings — mostly historic Class B and C structures with small enough floor plates for natural light — as candidates for the program.

The DRFD is a tax increment financing mechanism that directs increases in property tax revenue toward annual incentive payments for eligible conversion projects over a 30-year period. The district's boundaries include the Financial District, Union Square, and parts of SoMa and the Market Street corridor. City planners estimate the program could save developers between 10 and 20 percent on building and development costs — enough, officials hope, to make projects financially viable after years of stalled efforts.

San Francisco had seen zero major office-to-residential conversions in more than a decade before the legislation passed. Officials cited New York City's similar tax incentive, which led to the conversion of more than 12,000 housing units in lower Manhattan, as the model. If all 48 eligible buildings converted, city analysts say it could create roughly 4,400 new homes downtown.

The program is part of a broader downtown recovery push that also includes the expanded Downtown SF Partnership and new public realm investments along the Embarcadero. Cautious optimism is the prevailing tone among real estate observers, who note that the financing district is one critical piece of a larger, multi-pronged strategy.

events.title: ArtSpan 'Arrivals' Exhibition at the Ferry Building
events.location: Ferry Building Grand Hall, 1 Ferry Building, Embarcadero
events.description: ArtSpan and the Ferry Building present 'Arrivals,' a free Art-In-Neighborhoods exhibition showcasing work by six local artists whose lives and practices have been shaped by the immigrant experience. Featured media includes mixed-media prints, oil paintings, ceramics, and hand-pieced quilts.

events.title: The 49th Annual San Francisco Marathon
events.location: Start/Finish: Embarcadero at Mission St, Embarcadero
events.description: The full marathon (26.2 miles) starts at the Embarcadero, crosses the Golden Gate Bridge, and finishes back near the Bay Bridge; the event also offers half marathon, 10K, 5K, and ultra distances. Expect street closures along the Embarcadero from midnight through early afternoon.

events.title: Cinema on the Square: 'Pokémon: Detective Pikachu'
events.location: Union Square Plaza, 333 Post St, Union Square
events.description: The free outdoor summer movie series Cinema on the Square returns to Union Square Plaza with a screening of 'Pokémon: Detective Pikachu.' Pre-show activities including trivia, prizes, popcorn, and drinks begin two hours before sunset; all screenings are free.

events.title: Critical Mass Bicycle Ride
events.location: Embarcadero Plaza, foot of Market Street, Embarcadero
events.description: San Francisco's beloved monthly mass bicycle ride gathers at Embarcadero Plaza on the last Friday of every month — all cyclists welcome, no registration required. Expect significant traffic impacts throughout Downtown on Friday evening.

events.title: HEAD WEST Marketplace at the Ferry Building
events.location: Ferry Building Back Plaza, 1 Ferry Building, Embarcadero
events.description: The monthly outdoor marketplace returns to the Ferry Building's waterfront back plaza, featuring local makers, crafters, artists, vintage merchants, and live music — all free admission, kid- and pet-friendly.

events.title: S.F. Comedy Showcase at Punch Line
events.location: Punch Line Comedy Club, 444 Battery St, Financial District
events.description: The weekly SF Comedy Showcase spotlights a rotating lineup of local and touring stand-up comedians at one of the city's oldest comedy clubs. Two-drink minimum; tickets available at punchlinecomedyclub.com.

events.title: Exploratorium After Dark: Out of This World (Adults 18+)
events.description: The Exploratorium's adults-only Thursday night series features a full bar, live music, and special themed programming; this month's theme is space science and the search for extraterrestrial life, with SETI scientists on hand.

events.title: Walking Tour: Welcome to San Francisco
events.description: A guided walking tour starting at the Ferry Building and exploring the history and culture of downtown San Francisco's waterfront neighborhoods, presented through the Downtown SF Partnership's public programming calendar.

moreNews.headline: Japanese Sando & Matcha Shop Tadaima Coming to 113 Sacramento St.
moreNews.body: A new Japanese café called Tadaima is preparing to open at 113 Sacramento Street in the Financial District, according to What Now San Francisco citing the San Francisco Business Times. The shop will take over the former Orale Orale restaurant space and is expected to specialize in Japanese sandwiches (sandos) and matcha drinks. An opening date has not yet been announced.

moreNews.headline: Downtown SF Foot Traffic Up 34.7% Over Q4 2025, Partnership Reports
moreNews.body: The Downtown SF Partnership's latest foot-traffic data shows 2026 is off to a strong start, with nonresident district visits exceeding 10 million and average daily visits up 34.7% compared to the fourth quarter of 2025. The organization attributes the surge to major events and a wave of new ground-floor business openings across the Financial District and Jackson Square. The figures come as the Partnership prepares to launch its expanded district in January 2027.

moreNews.headline: Firework Explosion Near Sutter and Montgomery Draws Crowds, No Injuries
moreNews.body: First responders rushed to the intersection of Sutter and Montgomery streets in the Financial District on the evening of Monday, July 20, after reports of a loud explosion drew onlookers. Firefighters and police officers determined the source was a firework; no injuries were reported. The incident briefly disrupted foot traffic in the busy corridor during evening commute hours.

moreNews.headline: Union Square Powell Street Redesign on Track for Late 2026 Construction Start
moreNews.body: The Union Square Alliance reports that the Powell Street improvement project has entered its next design phase, with new renderings released and construction expected to begin in late 2026 and a ribbon-cutting planned for late 2027. The San Francisco Arts Commission approved the design in September. Alliance leadership credited Mayor Daniel Lurie and Supervisor Danny Sauter for their support in securing project funding.
moreNews.sourceName: Visit Union Square SF / Union Square Alliance

restaurants.name: Tadich Grill

restaurants.name: Sears Fine Food

restaurants.description: Pastry chef Belinda Leong's acclaimed patisserie brought its celebrated kouign-amann, croissants, and seasonal cakes to the Powell Street side of Union Square Plaza in 2025.

restaurants.name: Hog Island Oyster Co.

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
hotels.description: A dramatic Embarcadero Center tower with a soaring 17-story atrium lobby, Bay views, and direct access to shops and restaurants in the Embarcadero Center complex.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero
hotels.description: A Forbes five-star hotel occupying the upper floors of 757 Market Street with panoramic Bay and city views, a world-class spa, and the celebrated Oasia restaurant.

hotels.name: 1 Hotel San Francisco
hotels.description: A nature-inspired sustainable luxury hotel on the Embarcadero waterfront featuring 199 rooms, the Terrene restaurant, yoga programming, and panoramic Bay views steps from the Ferry Building.

hotels.name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
hotels.description: A 27-floor tower in the heart of the Financial District with stunning Bay views, 20,000 sq ft of event space, the 750 Restaurant & Bar, and easy walkability to Chinatown and the Embarcadero.

hotels.name: Club Quarters Hotel, Embarcadero
hotels.description: A members-friendly business hotel on the Embarcadero waterfront offering comfortable, no-frills accommodations convenient to the Financial District, Ferry Building, and Muni/BART.

hotels.name: Harbor Court Hotel San Francisco

hotels.name: The St. Regis San Francisco

hotels.name: Westin St. Francis

hotels.name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel

shops.name: The RealReal — Union Square Flagship

shops.name: Levi's Flagship San Francisco
shops.description: The global flagship of the iconic San Francisco-born denim brand, offering the full Levi's collection plus custom tailoring and the Tailor Shop for personalized alterations on Union Square.

shops.name: Nintendo Store San Francisco

shops.name: Maiden Lane Shops

shops.name: Ferry Building Marketplace

shops.name: Ferry Plaza Farmers Market

shops.name: Saks Fifth Avenue
shops.description: San Francisco's Saks Fifth Avenue flagship anchors the Union Square luxury shopping corridor with designer ready-to-wear, fine jewelry, beauty, and personal styling services.

shops.name: Neiman Marcus San Francisco

shops.name: Galerie Lassen

artEntertainment.name: Orpheum Theatre
